02 What We Designed: We ran a white laminate perimeter around three sides and dropped a blue carpet island inside it, so the 54 sqm booth read as a room rather than a corridor. Behind a horizontal slat screen sits a closed meeting room with a long timber table.

That split is what the exhibition stall design at LASER World of PHOTONICS Bengaluru was built around, and the raised blue platform kept the boundary obvious even when the aisle filled up.

title: NB Palm Exhibition Stall Design at Wedding Festival Ahmedabad 2026
design_style: Residential lounge with gold-framed gallery walls
materials_used: Cream painted wall panels | Gold-finish picture frames | Fluted timber counter fronts | Black ceiling track with spotlights | Linear crystal pendants | Ochre loop pile carpet | Backlit acrylic logo
special_features: Gold-framed amenity photo gallery | Backlit three-dimensional brand logo | Project journey wall with tower renders | Bar-height discussion tables | Lounge seating around a low table
01 The Challenge: The Wedding Festival is a banquet-hall show full of lehengas and jewellery, so a residential project stand had to work in a room where nobody arrives thinking about property. NB Palm needed the exhibition stall design at Wedding Festival Ahmedabad to feel like a sales lounge rather than a booth, inside 24 sqm with one open side.
02 What We Designed: We treated the single open face as a doorway into a room. Cream walls carry gold-framed photographs of the clubhouse, theatre and indoor games, hung the way pictures are hung in a home. A backlit logo sits above a screen on the centre wall, with the project journey mapped around it in circular badges. Ochre carpet, lounge seating, a low table and two bar-height tables complete it.
03 Why It Worked: Dressing the stand as a living space suited the audience, because couples planning a wedding are often also planning a first home, and they stayed seated long enough for a real conversation. Framed amenity photographs did more work than a floor plan, and the exhibition stall design at Wedding Festival Ahmedabad kept the 64% line readable from the corridor.
